subcompetencies.name: Gathers an Essential and Accurate Patient History

level_1: Acquires a basic rheumatic history
Independently requests additional information to supplement available medical records
level_2: Reviews available medical records
Integrates the current patient history with the complete medical record, supplemental information, and disease activity measures
level_3: Integrates a rheumatic history with a comprehensive medical history, including functional aspects
Identified as a role model in interpreting subtleties and resolving ambiguities in the patient history
level_4: Identifies relevant findings in the medical record
level_5: Acquires a tailored comprehensive rheumatic history, including historical subtleties and psychosocial aspects

level_1: Identifies the elements of a comprehensive physical examination
Performs a tailored comprehensive musculoskeletal examination including advanced techniques, when applicable
level_2: Identifies the elements of a musculoskeletal examination
Performs a tailored comprehensive physical examination that elicits subtle findings
level_3: Performs all elements of a comprehensive physical examination
Performs a tailored comprehensive musculoskeletal examination that elicits subtle findings
level_4: Performs all elements of a musculoskeletal examination
Identified as a role model for performing and interpreting a comprehensive, accurate physical and musculoskeletal examination
level_5: Performs a tailored comprehensive physical examination including advanced techniques, when applicable

level_1: With supervision, formulates a differential diagnosis for a patient
Independently develops a management plan for a patient with common disease presentations
Independently develops and implements a prioritized management plan with consideration of acuity and complexity of disease presentation
level_2: Demonstrates an awareness of disease activity measures
Independently formulates a prioritized differential diagnosis for typical disease presentations
Independently formulates a prioritized differential diagnosis with consideration of newly recognized and emerging conditions
level_3: With supervision, develops a management plan
Incorporates and interprets the results of disease activity measures
Identified as an expert resource for management of a focused disease area
level_4: Independently formulates a broad differential diagnosis for typical disease presentations
Independently recognizes disease acuity, and with supervision, develops a prioritized management plan
level_5: Identifies applicable disease activity measures
Independently formulates a prioritized differential diagnosis with consideration of typical and atypical disease presentations

level_1: Identifies indications and adverse effects of medications used to treat patients with common rheumatic conditions
Integrates best available evidence to prescribe, monitor, and assess the response to pharmacotherapy used in the management of patients with common and complex rheumatic conditions
level_2: Prescribes and monitors medications used in patients with common rheumatic conditions
Independently modifies treatment plans to address comorbidities
level_3: Evaluates for comorbidities that may alter therapeutic recommendations
Develops a clinical practice pathway for management of patients with rheumatic conditions
level_4: Prescribes, monitors, and assesses the response to pharmacotherapy used in the management of patients with common rheumatic conditions
level_5: Modifies treatment plans to address comorbidities, with supervision

level_1: Identifies indications for joint and soft tissue aspirations and injections, and discusses principles of informed consent
Independently performs common joint and soft tissue aspirations and injections
level_2: Performs common joint and soft tissue injections and aspirations with direct supervision, including independently discussing risks and benefits, obtaining informed consent, identifying anatomic landmarks, and demonstrating aseptic technique
Independently interprets the findings of musculoskeletal ultrasound for common conditions, and recognizes the role of ultrasound in non- musculoskeletal rheumatic conditions
level_3: Recognizes the role of musculoskeletal ultrasound in the diagnosis and treatment of patients with rheumatic conditions
Independently performs complex joint and soft tissue aspirations or injections, including unusual sites, anatomic abnormalities, or incorporating imaging guidance
level_4: Performs common joint and soft tissue aspirations and injections with indirect supervision
Independently performs and interprets point-of- care diagnostic ultrasound and uses ultrasound to guide invasive procedures
level_5: Interprets the findings of musculoskeletal ultrasound for common conditions with supervision

level_1: Respectfully receives a consultation request
Recognizes disease acuity and prioritizes management steps
level_2: With supervision, recognizes disease acuity
Integrates recommendations from different members of the health care team and effectively conveys consultative assessment and rationale to all health care team members
level_3: Clearly and concisely responds to a consultation request
Mobilizes resources to provide care in high- acuity situations
level_4: Independently recognizes disease acuity
Identified as a role model for the provision of consultative care across the spectrum of disease complexity and acuity
level_5: Verifies understanding of recommendations with the primary team when providing consultation

level_1: Identifies key features of common rheumatic conditions
Demonstrates in-depth knowledge of anatomy, genetics, immunology, metabolism, and other basic sciences pertaining to rheumatic conditions
level_2: Demonstrates basic knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and other basic sciences
Integrates knowledge of the pathogenesis, epidemiology, clinical expression, treatments, and prognosis of a broad range of rheumatic conditions
level_3: Demonstrates broad knowledge of common rheumatic conditions
Integrates knowledge of anatomy, genetics, immunology, metabolism, and other basic sciences pertaining to a broad range of rheumatic conditions
level_4: Demonstrates basic knowledge of anatomy, genetics, immunology, metabolism, and other basic sciences pertaining to rheumatic conditions
Identified as a subject matter expert in basic and/or clinical science of rheumatic conditions
level_5: Demonstrates knowledge of less common rheumatic conditions as well as common rheumatic conditions associated with higher complexity

level_1: Explains the rationale, risks, and benefits for common diagnostic testing in patients being evaluated for rheumatic conditions
level_2: Integrates value and test characteristics into diagnostic strategies in patients with uncomplicated rheumatic conditions
level_3: Integrates value and test characteristics into diagnostic strategies in patients with complex rheumatic conditions
level_4: Integrates and reconciles information, including non-specific and/or conflicting diagnostic test results to form a cohesive evaluation
level_5: Identified as an expert in testing strategies and in the selection and interpretation of complex, new, or emerging tests

level_1: Identifies areas worthy of scholarly investigation, with supervision
level_2: Designs a scholarly activity with a mentor(s)
level_3: Engages in scholarly work, incorporates feedback, and participates in critical appraisal and analysis of project data
level_4: Produces scholarly work suitable for dissemination as an abstract or presentation
level_5: Dissemination of independent scholarly work that has generated new medical knowledge, educational programs, or process improvement

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes quality improvement initiatives relevant to rheumatology practice
Discloses patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in quality improvement initiatives relevant to rheumatology practice
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (actual or simulated)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local population
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems including outpatient settings
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of their interprofessional teams
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Leads in the design and implementation of improvements to the care coordination process
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional teams
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
Leads innovations and advocates for populations and communities with health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the complex health care system (e.g., hospital, skilled nursing facility, finance, personnel, technology)
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Independently completes proper documentation and coding for a patient encounter
level_2: Recognizes the impact of cost and patient payment model on care decisions
Engages with patients in shared decision making and incorporates principles of high-value care into management plans
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care and transition of care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Demonstrates knowledge of current evaluation and management billing practices
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_4: Identify the principles of high-value care and delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transition of care
Educates others on proper documentation, billing, and coding practices
level_5: Demonstrates use of information technology (e.g., electronic health record) needed for clinical practice
Advocates for individual patient care needs to provide high-value care

level_1: Formulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences to inform care
level_2: Locates available evidence and incorporates patient preferences to inform patient care
level_3: Evaluates and applies best available evidence and incorporates patient preferences and values in order to provide care tailored to individual patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence, and recognizes gaps and conflicting evidence to guide care tailored to individual patients
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients; and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Commitment to Reflective Practice and Personal Growth

level_1: Establishes personal and professional goals, identifying gap(s) between goals and current performance
Seeks feedback consistently, and sustains behavioral change as necessary
level_2: Demonstrates receptiveness to feedback, analyzing and reflecting on factors contributing to gap(s) between goals and current performance
Uses data and feedback from multiple sources to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and when necessary, improves it
level_3: Designs and implements a learning plan, with prompting
Role models consistently seeking performance data with adaptability and humility, and coaches others on reflective practice
level_4: Seeks feedback episodically, and institutes behavioral change(s) when necessary
Facilitates the design and the implementation of learning plans for others
level_5: Independently creates and implements an individualized learning plan

level_1: Describes when and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses, including strategies for addressing common barriers
level_2: Identifies and describes triggers for professionalism lapses and takes responsibility for own professional behavior
level_3: Proactively recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses
level_4: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations and intervenes to prevent lapses in self and others
level_5: Coaches others when behavior fails to meet professional expectations

level_1: Performs tasks and responsibilities, with prompting
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_2: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities
Demonstrates leadership to ensure tasks and responsibilities are completed in a timely manner with attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with attention to detail in routine situations
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
Creates strategies to enhance others’ ability to efficiently complete tasks and responsibilities
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes status of own and others’ well- being, with assistance
With assistance, develops a plan to improve personal knowledge, skills, and attitudes
level_2: With assistance recognizes personal gaps in knowledge, skills, and attitudes
Independently recognizes the impact of own and others’ well- being on the patient and team, and asks for help when needed
level_3: Independently recognizes status of own and others’ well-being, and asks for help when needed
Independently implements a plan to improve personal knowledge, skills, and attitudes
level_4: Independently recognizes limits in personal knowledge, skills, and attitudes
Leads initiatives to improve wellness at the program or institutional level
level_5: Recognizes the impact of own and others’ well- being on the patient and team, with assistance
Coaches others when limitations in knowledge, skills, and attitudes do not meet professional expectations

level_1: Uses language and nonverbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
Adjusts communication strategies based on identified barriers, incorporating patient and caregiver expectations and goals of care
level_2: Recognizes common barriers to effective communication (e.g., language, disability) while accurately communicating own role within the health care system
Consistently establishes and maintains therapeutic relationships using shared decision making
level_3: Establishes a therapeutic relationship with the patient in uncomplicated clinical encounters using active listening and clear language
Uses self-reflection to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_4: Recognizes complex barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy)
Serves as a role model in establishing respectful, culturally sensitive therapeutic relationships while mitigating communication barriers
level_5: Establishes a therapeutic relationship with the patient in challenging clinical encounters

level_1: Uses language that is respectful and values all members of the health care team
Provides feedback to peers and other learners on the team
level_2: Accepts feedback from team members
Optimizes flexible communication strategies using input from all team members to build consensus and resolve conflicts, as needed
level_3: Communicates basic information effectively with all health care team members
Communicates detailed and effective feedback to any member of the health care team
level_4: Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Demonstrates leadership in promoting open and safe communication within and between teams
level_5: Communicates highly complex information effectively with all health care team members
Educates others in providing effective feedback

subcompetencies.name: Patient-Centered Interprofessional Communication within Health Care Systems

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record
Appropriately selects direct and indirect forms of communication based on context
level_2: Safeguards patient personal health information in direct (e.g., telephone, in- person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, text messages) communications
Communicates clearly, concisely, timely, and in an organized written form, including anticipatory guidance
level_3: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record
Produces written or verbal communication (e.g., patient notes, email) that could serve as an example for others to follow
level_4: Accurate and timely documentation with appropriate use of documentation tools
Participates in establishing communication tools or policies for the division, department, or institution
level_5: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
